method: Independent comparison of the exact Q16 and Q26 question wording, reader answer and same-question evidence, fixed answer key, and authoritative-source.txt. Reader support labels are not grades. No summary, other answers, prior grades, or adjudications were used to supply missing facts.

adjudications.reason: Every requested part is resolved: grain, cheese and wine qualify; wool does not; one food goes to the Goods Market; absent food, five coins are due, with torture for the shortfall if those coins cannot be paid. The question asks which goods qualify, the destination, and the no-food/fewer-than-five-coins branch. It does not separately ask whether to pay coins despite having wine. The final caveat expressly preserves the general rule already stated; it supplies neither a competing payment rule nor an exception. Its reservation about an additional scenario-specific pronouncement is incidental to these requested parts. Even applying the rule to the opening inventory needs no unstated fact: wine is identified as food and food payment precedes the conditional coin fallback.
adjudications.decisive_response_text: If unable to pay food, pay 5 coins; if unable to pay those coins, undergo torture for the shortfall. The summary does not specify whether coins are paid in this particular scenario beyond the general rule.
adjudications.same_question_evidence: Events — Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable, pay 5 coins; if unable, torture. Wool and brocade are not food.

source_references.text: Grain/cheese/wine qualify, wool does not. Must pay one food to Goods Market; if no food pay 5 coins, if unable undergo torture for missing coins.

You must pay 1 food item (grain, cheese, or wine). Return the paid food item to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay the food, pay 5 coins instead. If you cannot do this either, you must undergo torture (see below).

adjudications.reason: The answer specifies Knight + Scholar for Scriptorium and defines Town Hall activation as one or two eligible neutral Followers, with no printed profession restriction for Town Hall itself. Read together, that is a generic neutral-Follower requirement: it does not leave a profession to be selected from an unidentified restricted set. Neutral also excludes the colored starting Followers. The requested distinction is the professions allowed to activate Town Hall before substitutions or Technology; the answer resolves that through the unrestricted neutral category rather than enumerating professions. Its wording about the summary not specifying a printed restriction does not withdraw the positive generic activation rule. Exact profession matching on subsequent Beneficial Deed destinations is a source-backed limitation in the key, but the question does not request the destination procedure, and that limitation is not a printed profession requirement for activating Town Hall. No additional detail has been imported from another response.
adjudications.decisive_response_text: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall requires one or two eligible Followers; its two spaces take neutral Followers, and the summary does not specify a printed profession restriction for Town Hall itself.
adjudications.same_question_evidence: Actions table — Scriptorium and Town Hall; Town Hall section says place one or two neutral Followers.

source_references.text: Scriptorium Knight+Scholar. Town Hall one or two neutral Followers of any profession, but no colored starting Followers; Deed destinations must match exact depicted professions.

source_references.text: During the Planning Phase, you can place 1 or 2 Character Tiles in the Town Hall. (The Town Hall does not require both spaces be occupied in order to activate.) When using the “Town Hall” action, move one or both Character Tiles from the Town Hall to any free appropriate spaces on the “Beneﬁ cial Deeds” board.

You cannot replace the Character Tiles required for Beneﬁ cial Deeds with other tiles (like Monks). You must always use the exact Character Tiles as shown on the spaces. Character Tiles used for Beneﬁ cial Deeds remain there for the rest of the game. Please note: You may not place the Followers of your color (i.e. your initial Farmer, Boatman, Craftsman, and Trader) in the Town Hall.
